import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 8.52

by A. Yu. Olshanskii

(Well-known problem). Do there exist infinite finitely presented periodic groups?

A group is *periodic* (or a *torsion group*) if every element has finite order.
A group is *finitely presented* if it is isomorphic to a group given by finitely many
generators and finitely many defining relators, that is, to a quotient of a free group of
finite rank by the normal closure of a finite set.

The notebook cross-references Problem 6.3.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«8.52»

/--
Do there exist infinite finitely presented periodic groups?

Here a group $G$ is finitely presented if there are $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and a finite set of
relators $R \subseteq F_n$ in the free group on $n$ generators such that
$G \cong F_n / \langle\langle R \rangle\rangle$, and $G$ is periodic if every element of $G$
has finite order (`Monoid.IsTorsion G`).
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«8.52» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G), Infinite G ∧
      (∃ (n : ℕ) (rels : Finset (FreeGroup (Fin n))),
        Nonempty (PresentedGroup (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))) ≃* G)) ∧
      Monoid.IsTorsion G := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«8.52»
attempts.decomposition_objections: None. The single-slot decomposition (one yes/no existence question; parenthetical and cross-reference are remarks) is correct.
modeling_decisions: 'Finitely presented' has no Mathlib predicate for groups, so it is stated inline as `∃ (n : ℕ) (rels : Finset (FreeGroup (Fin n))), Nonempty (PresentedGroup (rels : Set _) ≃* G)`. Generators are indexed by `Fin n`; this is no loss of generality since any finite presentation on a finite generating type is isomorphic to one on `Fin n` via `PresentedGroup.equivPresentedGroup`, and both `Infinite` and `Monoid.IsTorsion` are invariant under `MulEquiv`.
The existential group lives in `Type` (universe 0), following the idiom of Kourovka/1_74.lean. Finitely presented groups are countable, so this is not a mathematical restriction.
'Periodic' is taken as `Monoid.IsTorsion G` (every element has finite order); no exponent bound is imposed, matching the notebook's unbounded 'periodic'.

Boundary check: `n = 0` yields the trivial group (finite), and an empty relator set yields a free group (torsion only if trivial), so the right-hand side cannot be trivially satisfied and genuinely constrains `answer(sorry)`.

The parenthetical '(Well-known problem)' and the cross-reference 'Compare with 6.3' are treated as remarks; the cross-reference is mentioned in the module docstring but the content of Problem 6.3 is not stated, since its text was not provided.

'Infinite' is `Infinite G`; 'periodic' is Mathlib's `Monoid.IsTorsion` (every element has finite order); 'finitely presented' is expressed inline with existing Mathlib primitives (`FreeGroup`, `PresentedGroup`, `Finset`, `MulEquiv`) as: isomorphic to the free group on `Fin n` modulo the normal closure of a finite relator set. `answer(True)` is the positive answer (such groups exist).

namespace Kourovka.«8.52»

/-- A group $G$ is *finitely presented* if it is isomorphic to a group
$\langle x_1, \dots, x_n \mid r_1, \dots, r_m \rangle$ with finitely many generators
and finitely many defining relations, i.e. to `PresentedGroup rels` for some
finite set `rels` of words in the free group on `Fin n`. -/
def IsFinitelyPresented (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (rels : Finset (FreeGroup (Fin n))),
    Nonempty (PresentedGroup (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))) ≃* G)

presented. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isFinitelyPresented_presentedGroup {n : ℕ} (rels : Finset (FreeGroup (Fin n))) :
    IsFinitelyPresented (PresentedGroup (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n)))) :=
  ⟨n, rels, ⟨MulEquiv.refl _⟩⟩

Here *periodic* means that every element has finite order (`Monoid.IsTorsion`), and

finitely many defining relations (`IsFinitelyPresented`).

    ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G), Infinite G ∧ IsFinitelyPresented G ∧ Monoid.IsTorsion G := by
  sorry

new_definitions.closest_existing_considered: `Group.FG` (only finite generation, too weak: finitely generated periodic infinite groups exist, e.g. Golod–Shafarevich/Grigorchuk groups, so using it would change the problem); `PresentedGroup` (used as the building block, but carries no finiteness condition on relators); `Algebra.FinitePresentation`/`Module.FinitePresentation` (ring/module notions, not groups).
new_definitions.name: Kourovka.«8.52».IsFinitelyPresented
new_definitions.why_needed: Neither Mathlib nor FormalConjecturesForMathlib has a predicate for a group being finitely presented (Mathlib has only `Group.FG`/`Monoid.FG` for finite generation and the constructor `PresentedGroup rels` without a finiteness predicate). Defined as `∃ (n : ℕ) (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))), rels.Finite ∧ Nonempty (PresentedGroup rels ≃* G)`, i.e. isomorphic to a group with finitely many generators and finitely many relators. A short proved `@[category API]` lemma `isFinitelyPresented_presentedGroup` (a `PresentedGroup` on `Fin n` with finite relator set is finitely presented) accompanies it.

kourovka.«8.52».why: Stated as `answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G), Infinite G ∧ IsFinitelyPresented G ∧ Monoid.IsTorsion G`. Periodicity is Mathlib's `Monoid.IsTorsion`; infinitude is `Infinite`; finite presentability has no Mathlib/repo predicate for groups, so a bespoke `IsFinitelyPresented` (isomorphic to `PresentedGroup rels` for a finite `rels ⊆ FreeGroup (Fin n)`) is defined in the file. The parenthetical '(Well-known problem)' and 'Compare with 6.3' are remarks only and are reproduced in the module docstring.
